FDA dims Bright Minds’ outlook with partial hold on seizure trial over toxicity in mice
summary: The FDA has put a partial hold on Bright Minds Biosciences’ seizure study application over preclinical toxicity data and concerns about its preparations for enrolling children.

title: Lower dose of Tiziana's MS drug reduces neuroinflammation, while higher dose struggles
summary: Tiziana Life Sciences’ intranasal drug has hit the dual endpoints of a phase 2a study in patients with a form of multiple sclerosis (MS), although the win was slightly marred by the higher dose missing on a key neuroinflammation goal.

title: The cost of waiting: What reaching clinical proof-of-concept sooner means for biotech cash burn
summary: Explore how delays before clinical proof-of-concept increase biotech cash burn, and how connected drug development can preserve capital and runway.

title: China's InventisBio delivers competitive TYK2 data in phase 3 psoriasis win
summary: A phase 3 trial of InventisBio’s nomelcitinib has hit its primary endpoint, delivering evidence that the TYK2 inhibitor can hold its own against rival psoriasis drugs.

title: Gilead reveals partial clinical hold on 2 CAR-T cell therapy trials
summary: Gilead Sciences announced on its third-quarter earnings call Oct. 29 that the company has placed a partial clinical hold on two studies for the CAR-T cell therapy KITE-753 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

title: When drug development gets personal
summary: When Third Rock Ventures partner Jigar Raythatha was diagnosed with brain cancer, he found himself relying on a drug originally developed by Agios, a biotech his firm backed years before he joined. On "The Top Line," he shares how the experience changed his perspective on drug development.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Lilly unifies global markets as 36-year vet Patrik Jonsson retires
summary: Lilly will unite its U.S. and international commercial units as a long-time exec retires. Enanta's CEO will hang up his hat after 23 year at the helm. Estrella has tapped a new a CEO to lead it through a clinical trial.

title: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility
summary: Bracco announced it will invest $230 million to establish its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media in Sanford, North Carolina.

title: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A
summary: Setara Biosciences, a privately held spinout formed following Jazz Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Actio Biosciences in September, has raised $90 million in series A financing to advance its clinical-stage neuroscience drug candidate and earlier-stage pipeline.

title: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline
summary: AstraZeneca has punted a pair of early-phase prostate cancer programs as part of its quarterly pipeline clear out.

title: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
summary: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.

title: Roche launches differential diagnosis test for mesothelioma
summary: Roche announced the global launch of its VENTANA BAP1 (SP527) test, an automated, ready-to-use immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.

title: Sanofi considering ‘moonshot’ treatments as M&A targets to survive Dupixent patent cliff
summary: Sanofi is considering “moonshot” treatments among the potential acquisition targets needed for the French pharma to urgently replenish its pipeline, Chief Financial Officer François-Xavier Roger told Fierce.

title: Molecular Partners to lay off up to 44% of workforce in radiotherapy pivot
summary: Molecular Partners plans to lay off up to 44% of its staff as it focuses its declining cash reserves on a radiotherapeutic pipeline led by an early-phase small cell lung cancer drug candidate.

title: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations
summary: Eli Lilly has dropped its phase 2 Alzheimer's disease program for mevidalen, marking another setback for the experimental drug as the Big Pharma expands its neuroscience pipeline through multibillion-dollar acquisitions.

title: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
summary: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

title: BMS walks away from $80M neurodegeneration bet after phase 1
summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has scrapped a phase 1 program it bet $80 million on just two years ago.

title: BioMarin inks up to $475M deal to challenge Fabry ERT incumbents
summary: BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront to license a Fabry disease drug candidate, expanding the franchise it acquired through its $4.8 billion takeover of Amicus Therapeutics.

title: Flagship brings 3 biotech platforms together to launch AI drug discovery player Etcelera
summary: Flagship Pioneering unveiled Etcelera today, a new AI-powered biotech emerging from stealth that aims to predict how potential medicines will act in patients.

title: Geron’s Rytelo stumbles in phase 3 as Novartis gears up for post-JAK inhibitor blood cancer bid
summary: Geron has discontinued a phase 3 trial of its Rytelo in JAK inhibitor-pretreated myelofibrosis after an independent data monitoring committee ruled that the study was unlikely to succeed, just as Novartis is gearing up for a delayed FDA approval bid for its pelabresib.

title: Oura, UC San Diego Health collaborate to study GLP-1 outcomes using continuous smart ring data
summary: Oura is pushing further into clinical healthcare research with its first clinical trial to study the link between smart ring data and obesity-treatment outcomes.

title: Ascletis’ challenger to Lilly’s Foundayo hits goals in phase 2 diabetes trial
summary: A phase 2 trial of Ascletis’ oral GLP-1 drug candidate has hit its primary and secondary endpoints, positioning the Chinese biotech to mount a two-front attack on Eli Lilly’s Foundayo.

title: Genmab's $8B Merus bet delivers as bispecific combo halves risk of death in phase 3
summary: Capping off a busy few days in Spain, Genmab reported results from the first interim analysis of a phase 3 trial showing that adding its bispecific antibody petosemtamab to Merck & Co.'s Keytruda cut the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

title: A multi-institutional investigation of psilocybin’s effects on mouse behavior
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02500-zIn a study across five independent labs, 2 mg kg−1 psilocybin in mice acutely increased avoidance-related behaviors in a robust, reproducible manner and acutely reduced fear expression, but previously reported persistent effects were modest or inconsistent.

title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-yThe serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02493-9The study shows that stimulus-specific neurons in the human amygdala determine which experiences become lasting memory, revealing a mechanism that predicts episodic memory formation and may guide future treatments for memory disorders.

title: Circuit mechanisms for disentangled representations and generalization in the hippocampus
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02491-xThe hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables, enabling flexible recombination and generalization to new situations. This code is supported by the geometry of population dynamics and cell–assembly interactions.

title: How Your Brain Saves Nostalgia From Scandals
summary: Can you separate the art from the artist? A new study shows our brains do it automatically: when a beloved creator falls from grace, memory performs "moral surgery," downgrading the person while protecting nostalgic memories of their art.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, cognitive dissonance, Memory, neurobiology, nostalgia, USF

title: Dietary Lecithin Linked to Lower Cognitive Impairment
summary: Can everyday dietary lecithin defend against memory loss? A study of 1,917 older adults combining MoCA assessments with targeted lipidomics reveals that lecithin and polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine are linked to lower rates of mild cognitive impairment, particularly in adults with lower education.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Aging, brain research, Chinese Medical Journal, cognition, dementia, diet, lecithin, MCI, neurobiology, Neurology

title: How to Map Brain Circuits Without Touching a Single Neuron
summary: How can scientists determine cause and effect when experiments are impossible? A new framework published in The Innovation uses delay embedding entropy to infer intervention-level causality directly from observational data, eliminating hidden confounders in neural circuits and complex systems.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain mapping, causality, Interventional Dynamical Causality, neurobiology

title: Overlooked Blood Cell May Tracks Parkinson’s Brain Changes
summary: Can blood platelets track Parkinson’s disease progression? Research from the Germans Trias i Pujol Research Institute (IGTP) demonstrates that platelets reflect neurodegenerative shifts—from mitochondrial breakdown to dementia onset—better than whole blood.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, brain research, Genetics, neurobiology, Parkinson's disease, platelets

title: Premature Birth Alters Cerebellar Wiring
summary: Why do premature infants face motor and language delays even without brain injuries? A landmark Science study led by Children's National reveals that developing outside the womb rewires the molecular programs of cerebellar Purkinje and granule cells, overturning the classic "catch-up" theory.
category: Featured, Neurology, brain development, brain research, cerebellum, developmental neuroscience, neurobiology, neurodevelopment, Neuroscience

title: New Transporter Bypasses Blood-Brain Barrier to Deliver Creatine
summary: How can drugs bypass the brain's tightest security checkpoint? Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland discovered that hijacking the sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter (SMVT) allows creatine derivatives to cross the blood-brain barrier, offering hope for rare deficiency syndromes.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, blood-brain barrier, brain research, creatine, drug delivery, neurobiology, Neurology, neuropharmacology, University of Eastern Finland

title: Living Near Industrial Water Polluters Linked to Higher Risk of PSP
summary: Can industrial water runoff trigger atypical parkinsonism? A 25-year study of 500,000 adults published in Neurology shows that living near facilities emitting pesticides, heavy metals, and organic pollutants is linked to a higher risk of progressive supranuclear palsy.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, AAN, brain research, environmental neuroscience, neurobiology, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, PSP, water pollution

title: Unreliable Labels Still Bias Decisions
summary: Do fact-checking badges stop bad information from swaying our minds? Cognitive psychology experiments reveal that even when a source is labeled as a 50% coin-flip, it still biases human choices, despite users knowing better.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, decision making, neurobiology, social behavior, social neuroscience, university of tskuba

title: Why Females Prefer Warmer Rooms
summary: Why do women generally prefer the thermostat set higher than men? Researchers at King’s College London discovered that two thermosensitive ion channels, TRPM2 and TRPM8, are molecularly tuned to activate at warmer temperatures in females, resolving a long-standing biological debate.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, brain research, King's College London, neurobiology, neuron, temperature, TRPM2, TRPM8

title: Why Some People Love Hugs While Others Hate Them
summary: Why do some hugs stay with us while others fade away? A survey of more than 15,000 UK adults published in PLOS One shows that 70% remember hugs for comfort, with empathy, relationship attachment styles, and body perception dictating how touch is stored in memory.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, brain research, emotion, emotional attachment, empathy, hugging, neurobiology, PLOS, social behavior, social neuroscience

title: Nearly Half of Distressed Adults Use AI for Therapy
summary: Are chatbots becoming informal therapists? A new study reveals that nearly half of adults experiencing severe psychological distress turn to generative AI tools for emotional support, raising urgent questions about clinical safety.
category: Featured, Neuroscience, Psychology, AI, Artificial Intelligence, brain research, LLMs, mental health, neurobiology, Neurotech, therapy

title: Breathing “Thin Air” May Protect Against Parkinson’s
summary: Can breathing thin mountain air help Parkinson's patients? Researchers demonstrated that 39 minutes of controlled intermittent hypoxia safely lowers stress hormones, raises anti-inflammatory adiponectin, and protects BDNF levels without disturbing sleep.
category: Featured, Neurology, Neuroscience, brain research, FAPESP, hypoxia, neurobiology, neuroinflammation, Parkinson's disease
